summary: Extends RESTCONF (RFC 8040) so it works with the Network Management Datastore Architecture from RFC 8342. It adds new datastore resources, a new query parameter, and requires servers that support the architecture to use the YANG library. It updates RFC 8040 and is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Imagine a control panel for a machine that used to show only one set of settings. This update adds more panels, such as saved settings and live settings, so a remote operator can look at each one separately.

subtitle: How RESTCONF servers expose the operational, running and intended datastores of the NMDA.

tldr.problem: RESTCONF as defined in RFC 8040 had no way to address the separate datastores of the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA), or to discover which datastores and modules a server supports.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds datastore resources under a new ds path, a with-origin query parameter, a changed meaning of with-defaults for the operational state datastore, and requires NMDA servers to use the YANG library.
tldr.outcome: RESTCONF clients can test for NMDA support, discover datastores and modules, and read or write each datastore. The change is backwards compatible with RFC 8040 because only new resources are added.

today: RFC 8527 is a Proposed Standard from March 2019 that updates RFC 8040, and nothing has obsoleted or updated it.

sections.title: Extending RESTCONF for the NMDA
sections.content:
This document extends the RESTCONF protocol of RFC 8040 to support the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA) of RFC 8342. It updates RFC 8040 so that RESTCONF clients can discover which datastores a server supports, determine which modules each datastore supports, and interact with all datastores of the NMDA.

The update introduces new datastore resources, adds a new query parameter, and requires RESTCONF servers that implement the NMDA to use the YANG library of RFC 8525. The solution is backwards compatible with RFC 8040 because it only adds new resources and leaves the semantics of existing ones unchanged.
sections.eli5: RESTCONF is a way to read and change a device's settings over the web. This RFC teaches it to handle the device's several kinds of settings lists, not just one.

sections.title: Datastore and YANG Library Requirements
sections.content:
An NMDA-compliant RESTCONF server MUST support the operational state datastore and MUST implement at least revision 2019-01-04 of the ietf-yang-library module from RFC 8525.

A server signals NMDA support both by implementing the {+restconf}/ds/ietf-datastores:operational resource and by implementing that YANG library revision. A client can test for support by sending HEAD or GET to that resource, and can then read the YANG library information from the operational state datastore to learn which datastores and modules the server supports.
sections.eli5: A device that speaks the new language must keep a live-settings panel and a list of what it can do. A client checks for the panel to find out if the device is new enough.

sections.title: The New Datastore Resources
sections.content:
Datastores are reached with the path template {+restconf}/ds/<datastore>. The datastore component is encoded as an identityref using the JSON encoding rules of RFC 7951, in the namespace-qualified form. The identity MUST derive from the datastore identity in the ietf-datastores module.

  • ietf-datastores:operational is the operational state datastore.
  • ietf-datastores:running is the running configuration datastore.
  • ietf-datastores:intended is the intended configuration datastore.

An NMDA-compliant server MUST implement the operational resource; the others MAY be implemented. YANG actions can only be invoked in the operational datastore. A datastore defined elsewhere, such as ds-ephemeral in a module example-ds-ephemeral, would appear at {+restconf}/ds/example-ds-ephemeral:ds-ephemeral.
sections.eli5: Each kind of settings list gets its own address, like separate doors labeled live, saved and planned. Only the live door has to exist.

sections.title: Protocol Operations on Datastores
sections.content:
The operations on the new resources are the same as those RFC 8040 defines for {+restconf}/data, with some exceptions. Dynamic configuration datastores are excluded, because each one needs review for the operations it supports. Some datastores are read-only by nature, such as intended, so an attempt to modify them fails: the server MUST return 405 Method Not Allowed with error-tag operation-not-supported. Paragraph 3 of Section 3.5.4 of RFC 8040 does not apply under {+restconf}/ds.

The with-defaults parameter also behaves differently on the operational state datastore, as covered in the next section.
sections.eli5: Most things you can do on the old panel work on the new ones. But if a panel is look-only, trying to change it gets a polite no.

sections.title: The with-defaults and with-origin Parameters
sections.content:
Support for with-defaults on the operational datastore is OPTIONAL and is announced by the capability URI urn:ietf:params:restconf:capability:with-operational-defaults:1.0. With no parameter, or with explicit, report-all or report-all-tagged, the server returns the in-use values, even where a YANG default is being used. With report-all-tagged, values matching the schema default get extra metadata. With trim, in-use values are returned but those matching the schema default are filtered out. An unsupported value is handled as in RFC 8040.

A new with-origin query parameter is added to GET. It asks the server to include origin metadata annotations, which show the source of each operational value. It is valid only on the operational datastore or datastores derived from it; otherwise the server MUST return 400 Bad Request with error-tag invalid-value. Annotations are not sent unless requested, and may be omitted on a child node whose value matches its parent. Support is OPTIONAL and is identified by urn:ietf:params:restconf:capability:with-origin:1.0.
sections.eli5: Two optional switches: one chooses whether default values are shown, and one asks the device to say where each live value came from.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The lowest RESTCONF layer is HTTPS, and the mandatory-to-implement secure transport is TLS (RFC 8446). RESTCONF uses the network configuration access control model of RFC 8341 to restrict users to a subset of operations and content. The security constraints of the base protocol, in Section 12 of RFC 8040, apply to the new datastore resources.

IANA registers two capability identifiers in the RESTCONF Capability URNs registry: :with-origin and :with-operational-defaults, with the URNs shown above.
sections.eli5: The new panels use the same locks as the old one, so only people allowed to look can look.
